chunks: 5901 - Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Murazim, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

When the child settles in his mother's womb, if it is a male, his face is turned toward his mother's back; and if it is a female, her face is turned toward her mother's belly. His hands are upon his cheeks, and his chin is upon his knees, in the posture of one sorrowful and distressed. He is like one tightly bound, attached by an intestine-like cord from his navel to his mother's navel. Through that navel-cord he is nourished from his mother's food and drink until the appointed time of his birth. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends to him an angel, who writes upon his forehead: wretched or felicitous, believer or disbeliever, rich or poor; and he writes his term, his sustenance, his illness, and his health. When the decreed sustenance for him from his mother's navel is cut off, the angel gives him a push, so he turns in alarm from that push, and his head comes to face the exit. When he falls upon the earth, he is driven into a tremendous terror and painful suffering. If a wind touches him or a hand touches him, he feels from that pain like the one whose skin has been flayed from him. He hungers but cannot seek food, thirsts but cannot seek water, and feels pain but cannot seek aid. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, appoints for him—through His mercy, compassion toward him, and love for him—his mother, who protects him from heat and cold with her own self, and nearly ransoms him with her soul. Out of tenderness toward him, she reaches a state in which she does not care to go hungry if he is full, to go thirsty if he is quenched, or to go unclothed if he is clothed. Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, places his sustenance in his mother's two breasts: in one of them is his drink, and in the other his food. Then when he suckles, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings him each day what He has decreed for him therein of sustenance. When he matures, He makes him understand family, wealth, voracity, and greed. Yet along with that he is exposed to afflictions, disabilities, and tribulations from every side. The angels guide him and direct him, while the devils lead him astray and seduce him. So he is perishing unless Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saves him. And Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, has mentioned the origin of the human being in the decisive part of His Book, and He, Mighty and Majestic, said:

"And certainly We created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a drop in a firm lodging. Then We created the drop into a clot; then We created the clot into a lump; then We created the lump into bones; then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators. Then after that, you shall surely die. Then on the Day of Resurrection you shall surely be raised."

Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, this is our condition; then how is your condition and the condition of the awsiya' after you in birth?" So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله remained silent for a long while, then said:

"O Jabir, you have asked about a tremendous matter that none can bear except one possessing a great share. Indeed, the Prophets and the awsiya' are created from the light of the greatness of Allah, Glorious is His praise. Allah places their lights in pure loins and pure wombs, guarding them with His angels, nurturing them with His wisdom, and feeding them with His knowledge. Their affair is too majestic to be described, and their states are too subtle to be known, because they are Allah's stars in His earth, His standards among His creation, His vicegerents over His servants, His lights in His lands, and His proofs over His creation. O Jabir, this is of the hidden knowledge and its stored treasure, so conceal it except from its people."

key_terms.الرِّزْقُ الْمُقَدَّرُ: the sustenance divinely apportioned and decreed
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءَ: the successors appointed after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.سُرَّتِهِ: his navel, referring here to the connection of fetal nourishment
key_terms.نُورِ عَظَمَةِ اللَّهِ: the light of Allah’s greatness from which the Prophets and awsiya' are described as created

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe human creation, divine decree, and the birth-status of the Prophets and awsiya'?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the stages of the human being from the womb through birth and early dependence, emphasizing divine decree, human vulnerability, and Allah’s mercy manifested through the mother’s care. It then distinguishes the Prophets and the awsiya' as beings whose origin and protection are of a unique luminous order, presenting their station as part of hidden divine knowledge.
